jobs.title: Drift Wood #30 · the Crab Derby, ii
jobs.prompt: a four-panel comic strip laid out as a two-by-two grid on a half page, thin black panel borders (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, drawn the same in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 19, gaunt boy drawn a head too tall, oversized thrift-store wool overcoat to the knee worn indoors, faded black tee, dark jeans, sneakers, a bristol pad clutched flat to his chest, chin up; GULLY — aged 20, stocky boy with a round face, backwards blue cap, faded green hoodie with his hands in the front pocket, muddy tan work boots, easy slouch. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: Fifteenth annual. The uncle wants the same crab. Wood wants to grow. Panel 1: an older fisherman tapping a weathered year-old flyer with a large crab on a shingle shack wall, two teenagers beside him (in this panel: WOOD, GULLY). Uncle says "Same crab. Change the number. Fifteen.". Panel 2: a teenage boy in an overcoat with a hand to his chest, wounded, proposing something to a fisherman (in this panel: WOOD). Wood says "An artist doesn't repeat himself. This year the crab could be seen from below. Looming. A crab of consequence.". Panel 3: a fisherman's flat face with a boy in a backwards cap behind him shaking his head in warning (in this panel: GULLY). Uncle says "Same crab. Twenty bucks.". Panel 4: two nearly identical crab flyers side by side on a shingle wall, the newer one more finely hatched, a boy in a backwards cap leaning in to compare them (in this panel: GULLY). Gully says "...You changed it.". Wood says "I changed nothing. Twenty bucks.". Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @gully_17 is the model sheet for GULLY: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Match the attached references: @gully_17 for the character the strip's Gully at 17; @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17; @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23.
